# p_a1b2 — Synchronized WFH; shared meals; shared TV

Both residents work from home in lockstep, 9:00 to 17:30 on weekdays, each at their own desk. They eat together at the kitchen table at 12:15 and 18:30. In the evening they watch TV on the couch from 20:00 to 22:00, sharing the blanket and the remote. On weekends they sleep in until 10:00, do errands 12:00–14:00 (one or both leave with keys and jackets), then are home the rest of the day. Marco runs twice a week (Tue, Thu) at 6:30, before work. He meditates on weekday evenings 19:00–19:45 in the bedroom. Omar reads on the armchair 22:00–23:00 before bed. Nothing of value leaves the house except keys, wallets, and outerwear during errands or lunch-outs.

What sets this apart: the kitchen table is occupied with plates and glasses at exactly 12:15 and 18:30 on weekdays; the TV stand remote migrates to the coffee table at 20:00; the meditation cushion is on the bedroom floor 19:00–19:45 weekdays. What would refute it: the remote still on the TV stand at 20:30 on a weekday, or the kitchen table empty at 18:30 on a Tuesday.
